title: State of Restaurant Operations 2026

history.reason: Read (benchmark PDF) during the first discovery session (issue #7)

source_type: industry benchmark survey report (n=112 restaurant leaders, early 2026)
reliability: Near-primary industry survey with stated sample and method. Fourth sells restaurant operations software and the report uses Fourth's own maturity framework; respondents are executives/owners, skewing multi-unit (over half oversee 20+ locations).
findings: 44% of operators report general managers spending six or more hours per week on unplanned administrative work (call-outs, payroll errors, last-minute schedule changes).

Top drivers of inventory variance: waste or spoilage 54%, receiving/counting errors 37%, recipe/portion non-compliance 29%, vendor/supply disruptions 29%, theft/loss/unrecorded usage 27%, inaccurate forecasting/ordering 26%.
Operators with under 5% sales forecast variance are far more likely to report under five unplanned admin hours per week (74%) than operators with 16%+ variance (22%).
Unplanned admin load tracks manager retention: 5% of low-admin operators report high GM/AGM turnover versus 15% among those with 6-10 unplanned hours.
64% of operators have not deployed AI or automation tools for operations.
limitations: Small sample (n=112) of leaders, not front-line managers; skews to multi-unit brands, so single-unit independent restaurants are underrepresented.
Self-reported, scored with the vendor's own maturity framework.
Inventory-specific hours are not separated from other unplanned admin in this report.
